#Side Note
. Alfama basically wasted bitrates on mistakenly boosted gamma and ignorant encoding configuration, yielding the worse video of all three -- less details in majority of the frames and bandings/blockings everywhere.
. (Therefore frame type of FRA in screenshots would never bother me.)
. Background footage of the final scrolling end credits in Alfama's video is upscaled and slightly zoomed in.
. Background footages of the static credits preceding to the final are upscaled (2929 frames) in all three releases.
. Arrow achieved slightly but appreciably better grain preservation than Kino, and a tad more details in a couple of scenes.
. Arrow's is a little bit off white/black balance in most frames with pale purplish tint, while Alfama's simply deviates to green. Kino did it perfectly.
. Dark areas in most frames of Arrow's are a bit unusually glossy.
. Arrow and Kino have lots of random luma bandings/blockings in dark areas, most of which are moderate and in different scenes.
. A few dark scenes from Kino and Arrow suffer chroma blockings/bandings/bars and at least one scene from Arrow suffers chroma fuck-up (horizontal green bars, check the last group of pic, can be easily eliminated though).
. (Consequently my encode just started with Arrow's luma and Kino's chroma.)

#Side Note
. Alfama's audio came with the only goodness of its (hopefully) intact pitch with original 24fps, but all the drawbacks such as 16-bit output with unshaped dither, sterile directionality and ridiculously unbalanced mixing have destroyed it.
. Kino and Arrow shared approximately the same master (occasionally with subtle differences in compression and sample counts of marginal sections) except that Arrow had 6.84 seconds longer sound of rain at the very end of End Credits (apart of initial and final blank samples ofc).



c) Stereo mix Waveform&Spectrum - Arrow's downmix vs. Kino's exclusive mix 

USA_2 | GBR_6_2_0.7071B* | GBR_6_2_B* | GBR_6_2_DplII | GBR_C_adapt_2 | GBR_L_adapt_2


#Side Note
. Presented with 11-minute excerpts from Arrow and Kino (57:17.210 to 1:08:07.253 in Arrow's timecode). GBR_*_adapt_2 refers to separated center and left channel from Arrow after duplication and level match for a bit (or no) more indication.
. Pictures tell little though.
. In fact Kino's additional stereo mix just sounds better than any common style of downmix from the 6ch track -- more natural, immersed and brisk. Thanks to some proper EQ applied to C channel (principally refers to dialogues as I assume it's sourced from a finished track) and (presumably) efforts on other elements to rectify stereo image.

BTW, to be more specific in case anyone might be in doubt, since 3.28 eac3to's standard downmix matrix for simple-stereo output is merely the same as default behaviours of many other ffmpeg-based fltp implementations, compliant to ITU-R BS.775-3:
# for 3/2/0 or 3/2/1 input without potential for clipping #  
FL' = FL + 0.707107*FC + 0.707107*BL | FR' = FR + 0.707107*FC + 0.707107*BR
which shall attenuate all channels involved except L&R by ~3dB.
Check eac3to's changelog, do some tests and forget about the outdated table.



d) Chapters & Subtitle(s)

. Only Kino had chapters named and differently segmented.
. All English ones are identical, contributed by Daniel Bird. Kino just applied edge blur, merged a bunch of lines, and removed the credits line at the end.
. Alfama's French sub is only for eight lines of English speech, and not forced.



e) Bonus Materials

. Kino has an outstanding commentary by Daniel Bird.
. Arrow rigs a load more bonus desserts with English subtitles, which is great despite of blunt upscaling of interlaced footage with jaggies and moire patterns.
. Kino provides HD only, sometimes oversharpened, but firmly with higher quality on clips that shared same footages with Arrow's.



f) Menu & Cover Art


. That's why I was driven to Kino's release in the first place.
